_doc: Guard Conformance Registry (superscar #3 — over/under-match). Maps EVERY live textual guard to its GUILT proof (the guard fires on the historical bad case) and INNOCENCE proof (the guard does NOT fire on the adjacent legitimate case). Enforced by infra/guard-conformance/check_guard_conformance.py: a censused guard missing from here, a phantom test reference, or a test no CI workflow runs = FAIL. The mandate rule this executes: 'nessuna guardia mergiata senza un test di innocenza E di colpevolezza' (cicatrix-superscar.md #3). To add a guard: write both tests first, then register it here.

_is_remote_dispatch.note: W92 (2026-07-11): the SAME function, previously wired only into the git-verb channel (W83), is now ALSO consulted by _write_hits_main — a 5th over-match of this guard was the file-write channel having zero remote-dispatch awareness at all. Direct unit coverage of _is_remote_dispatch itself stays owned by test_w83_remote_dispatch.py; the NEW call site's outcome is proven by test_w92_remote_write_dispatch.py under the _write_hits_main entry below. SUPERSEDED as a whole-command decision (6th over-match, same day, PR-gate finding): both call sites now use the SEGMENT-SCOPED `_is_position_remote_dispatched` instead — see that symbol below.

_is_position_remote_dispatched.note: 6th over-match (2026-07-11, found at PR-2266 gate before merge, same session as W92): `_is_remote_dispatch` was a WHOLE-COMMAND exemption on both channels — `ssh pro hostname && git pull origin main` and `ssh mini hostname && cp /tmp/x scripts/f.py` both got wrongly exempted because SOME segment (the prelude) was remote, even though the mutating verb/write-target lived in a LATER, LOCAL segment. Fix: `_segments()` splits the noise-stripped command on `&& || ; |`; this function answers whether the segment CONTAINING a given character offset is itself remote-dispatched. Both `_git_verb_verdict` and `_write_hits_main` now check every match/target against its OWN segment via `all(...)`/per-target loop, not the whole command. Direct-mention coverage stays owned by test_segment_scoped_dispatch.py's module docstring + `_write_hits_main`'s per-target loop (which mentions it by name); guard_fuzz_harness.py's outcome-level proof lives under `_git_verb_verdict`/`_write_hits_main` below (it never calls this symbol directly, only through those).

_git_verb_verdict.note: Pure decision function extracted from main() during the 6th-over-match fix (2026-07-11) SPECIFICALLY so guard_fuzz_harness.py can call the REAL logic instead of re-implementing it. The harness's ORIGINAL run_corpus() had hand-copied the git-verb decision path inline — that copy used the pre-fix whole-command `_is_remote_dispatch` check and drifted from `main()` the same day it was written, producing 24 false mismatches against cases the real guard already handled correctly. A fuzz harness testing its own stale reimplementation instead of the guard is the exact failure this tool exists to prevent; extracting a single callable source-of-truth closes that structurally, not just for today's drift.

_write_hits_main.note: W92 fix 2026-07-11: an ssh/scp/rsync-dispatched write with a RELATIVE destination used to resolve against the LOCAL session cwd, producing a phantom write-target into the main checkout for a write that never touches this machine. Fixed by consulting _is_remote_dispatch upstream of target extraction (same reuse discipline as the git-verb channel). 6th over-match (SAME session, PR-gate finding): the exemption was whole-command — now `_extract_write_targets` returns `(path, offset)` and each target is segment-scoped individually via `_is_position_remote_dispatched`.

infra/claude-hooks/guard_fuzz_harness.py.note: Reusable property/fuzz corpus runner for worktree_isolation.py's two decision channels (git_verb + write_target) — 445 generated command shapes (quotes, comments, newlines, heredocs, pipes, ssh-wrapping, git-verbs-inside-strings, true-compound remote-prelude-plus-local-mutation) classified against a fixture, not a hand-picked example list. Self-executing: `python3 infra/claude-hooks/guard_fuzz_harness.py` exits 1 on any unexplained mismatch. Guard-agnostic design (Case/run_corpus) intended for reuse by a future guard's own corpus generator. STRUCTURAL FIX (2026-07-11, 6th over-match): run_corpus's git_verb branch now calls `mod._git_verb_verdict()` directly instead of re-implementing the decision inline — the inline copy had drifted from the real guard the same day it was written (see _git_verb_verdict's registry note).
